description: beta-decay flips ONE quark, which retypes TWO of a nucleon's three pair-crossings, each by the same central scalar s = -h/2. Delta is therefore an exact three-term expansion s(S_A + S_B) + s^2 S_AB in the proton word with one and both flavour crossings smoothed, verified to 60 dps. Corrects this author's earlier one-letter claim, which CHECK 4 refutes numerically. Changes no number.

caveats: 🛑 CORRECTION OF THIS AUTHOR'S OWN EARLIER CLAIM. PR #7212's title, body, the Lean docstring and a comment on this PR all said the two nucleon words 'differ in exactly one letter: a single sigma becomes a single sigma^-1'. Wrong at the letter level. The COUNTS it was read off -- (1,2,0) vs (0,2,1) -- are correct and unchanged; the reading was wrong because the preserved ud count is a cancellation, not an absence of change. CHECK 4 refutes the one-letter reading numerically rather than merely retracting it.
Changes no number. The residual is -15.451387 %, identical to the merged Option-E witness, because this is an exact rewriting of the same element rather than a new model. Nothing downstream moves.

Scope-(a): measured on the census typed-crossing multisets in the gen-grouped ordering. two_shift_expansion is proved for ANY two slots carrying a common central shift; that the nucleon words are in that shape is read off _GEN_CHAINS and re-verified here, not proved.

The expansion does NOT reduce the open question to a solved one. It restates Delta in terms of 10- and 9-crossing traces; whether those are more tractable, or connect to the mass channel's own words, is not claimed.
